title: A formally unramified morphism has a universal first order thickening, unique up to unique isomorphism
statement: Let $h:Z\to X$ be a formally unramified morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism]. Then there exists a universal first order thickening $Z\subset Z'$ of $Z$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]. It is unique up to unique isomorphism: if $(Z'_1,i_1:Z\to Z'_1,h'_1:Z'_1\to X)$ and $(Z'_2,i_2,h'_2)$ are two universal first order thickenings of $Z$ over $X$, there is exactly one morphism $\varphi:Z'_1\to Z'_2$ with $h'_2\circ\varphi=h'_1$ and $\varphi\circ i_1=i_2$, and $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), with the uniqueness remark of Section 04F2 (section-universal-thickening), opening paragraph

proof.text: *Uniqueness.* If $(Z'_1,i_1,h'_1)$ and $(Z'_2,i_2,h'_2)$ are universal first order thickenings of $Z$ over $X$, there is exactly one $\varphi:Z'_1\to Z'_2$ with $h'_2\circ\varphi=h'_1$ and $\varphi\circ i_1=i_2$, and it is an isomorphism: this is the uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening], proved there by applying the universal property of each $Z'_k$ to the thickening $Z\subset Z'_l$ with $a=\mathrm{id}_Z$. It remains to prove existence.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Section 04F2 (section-universal-thickening), opening paragraph ('Thus if a universal first order thickening exists, then it is unique up to unique isomorphism'); proof of Lemma 04F3, second paragraph, first sentence

proof.text: *Affine pieces.* Choose an open covering $Z=\bigcup_{i\in I}Z_i$ by affine opens such that each $h(Z_i)$ lies in an affine open $U_i\subseteq X$: cover $X$ by affine opens $U$, and each open $h^{-1}(U)$ by affine opens of $Z$, affine opens forming a basis of the topology of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-open-restriction] the restriction $h_i:Z_i\to U_i$ is formally unramified. Write $U_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, $Z_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $R_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$, $S_i=\mathcal O_Z(Z_i)$, so that $h_i$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $\varphi_i=h_i^\sharp:R_i\to S_i$; by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-formally-unramified-iff-ring] $\varphi_i$ is a formally unramified ring map. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-universal-first-order-thickening] there is a surjection of $R_i$-algebras $\pi_i:S'_i\to S_i$ with square-zero kernel and the universal property for square-zero ideals, and by [lem-weil-pbc-universal-thickening-affine-case] $Z_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_i\subset Z'_i:=\operatorname{Spec}S'_i$, with closed immersion $\iota_i:Z_i\to Z'_i$ ($\operatorname{Spec}\pi_i$ composed with the identification) and $h'_i:Z'_i\to U_i$, is a universal first order thickening of $Z_i$ over $U_i$ (transporting along the isomorphisms $Z_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_i$, $U_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ only renames the objects in [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]). By part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-universal-thickening-open-pieces], composing $h'_i$ with the inclusion $U_i\subseteq X$, $Z_i\subset Z'_i$ is a universal first order thickening of $Z_i$ over $X$; we write $h'_i:Z'_i\to X$ from now on.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F3, third paragraph (affine case, from Algebra Lemma 04EB) and fourth paragraph, first three sentences (covering, Lemma 02HC, 'By the general remarks above Z_i ⊂ Z'_i is also a universal first order thickening of Z_i over X'); More on Morphisms, Lemma 02HD for the ring map

proof.text: *Overlaps.* For $i,j\in I$ put $Z_{ij}=Z_i\cap Z_j$, open in $Z_i$. Since $\iota_i$ is a homeomorphism of underlying spaces (a first order thickening is a thickening, [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (1)-(2)), there is a unique open subscheme $Z'_{ij}\subseteq Z'_i$ with $\iota_i^{-1}(Z'_{ij})=Z_{ij}$; $Z'_{ii}=Z'_i$. By part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-universal-thickening-open-pieces] (with $V=Z_{ij}$, $U=X$) both $Z_{ij}\subset Z'_{ij}$ (closed immersion $\iota_i|$, structure $h'_i|$) and $Z_{ij}\subset Z'_{ji}$ (closed immersion $\iota_j|$, structure $h'_j|$) are universal first order thickenings of $Z_{ij}$ over $X$. By the uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening] there is exactly one morphism $\varphi_{ij}:Z'_{ij}\to Z'_{ji}$ with $h'_j\circ\varphi_{ij}=h'_i|_{Z'_{ij}}$ and $\varphi_{ij}\circ\iota_i|_{Z_{ij}}=\iota_j|_{Z_{ij}}$, and it is an isomorphism; $\varphi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ because the identity has these properties. On underlying sets $\varphi_{ij}(\iota_i(z))=\iota_j(z)$ for $z\in Z_{ij}$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F3, fourth paragraph ('Let Z'_{i,j} ⊂ Z'_i be the open subscheme ... there is a canonical isomorphism φ_ij : Z'_{i,j} → Z'_{j,i} inducing the identity on Z_i ∩ Z_j')

proof.text: *Cocycle condition* (omitted in the source; its hint is carried out). Fix $i,j,k$ and $Z_{ijk}=Z_i\cap Z_j\cap Z_k$. The open $Z'_{ij}\cap Z'_{ik}\subseteq Z'_i$ is the open with $\iota_i^{-1}(Z'_{ij}\cap Z'_{ik})=Z_{ijk}$, so by part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-universal-thickening-open-pieces] it is a universal first order thickening of $Z_{ijk}$ over $X$, and likewise $Z'_{ji}\cap Z'_{jk}\subseteq Z'_j$ and $Z'_{ki}\cap Z'_{kj}\subseteq Z'_k$. (a) Since $\varphi_{ij}(\iota_i(z))=\iota_j(z)$ and these opens have the underlying sets $\iota_i(Z_{ijk})$, $\iota_j(Z_{ijk})$, $\varphi_{ij}^{-1}(Z'_{ji}\cap Z'_{jk})=Z'_{ij}\cap Z'_{ik}$. (b) The two morphisms $\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ij}$ and $\varphi_{ik}$, restricted to $Z'_{ij}\cap Z'_{ik}$, both land in the open $Z'_{ki}\cap Z'_{kj}$ (by (a) for the pairs $(j,k)$ and $(i,k)$), so they factor through it as morphisms of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion]; both satisfy $h'_k\circ(-)=h'_i|$ and $(-)\circ\iota_i|_{Z_{ijk}}=\iota_k|_{Z_{ijk}}$. Applying the universal property of $Z_{ijk}\subset Z'_{ki}\cap Z'_{kj}$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening] to the first order thickening $Z_{ijk}\subset Z'_{ij}\cap Z'_{ik}$ over $X$ (structure morphism $h'_i|$) and $a=\mathrm{id}_{Z_{ijk}}$, at most one morphism has these two properties, so $\varphi_{ik}=\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ij}$ on $Z'_{ij}\cap Z'_{ik}$. Hence $(Z'_i,Z'_{ij},\varphi_{ij})$ is glueing data of schemes.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F3, fourth paragraph ('We claim that these morphisms satisfy the cocycle condition ... Verification omitted. Hint: Use that Z'_{i,j} ∩ Z'_{i,k} is the universal first order thickening of Z_i ∩ Z_j ∩ Z_k'); glueing data as in Schemes, Section 01JA

proof.text: *Glueing.* By [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] there are a scheme $Z'$ and open immersions $\psi_i:Z'_i\to Z'$ with $Z'=\bigcup_i\psi_i(Z'_i)$, $\psi_i(Z'_{ij})=\psi_i(Z'_i)\cap\psi_j(Z'_j)$ and $\psi_i|_{Z'_{ij}}=\psi_j\circ\varphi_{ij}$. Put $W_i=\psi_i(Z'_i)$. The morphisms $h'_i\circ\psi_i^{-1}:W_i\to X$ agree on $W_i\cap W_j=\psi_i(Z'_{ij})$ because $h'_j\circ\varphi_{ij}=h'_i|_{Z'_{ij}}$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] they glue to $h':Z'\to X$ with $h'\circ\psi_i=h'_i$. The morphisms $\psi_i\circ\iota_i:Z_i\to Z'$ agree on $Z_{ij}$ because $\psi_j\circ\iota_j|_{Z_{ij}}=\psi_j\circ\varphi_{ij}\circ\iota_i|_{Z_{ij}}=\psi_i\circ\iota_i|_{Z_{ij}}$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] they glue to $\iota:Z\to Z'$ with $\iota|_{Z_i}=\psi_i\circ\iota_i$. Then $h'\circ\iota=h$, since on each $Z_i$ both equal $h'_i\circ\iota_i=h|_{Z_i}$ (uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]); i.e. $\iota$ is a morphism over $X$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base].

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F3, fourth paragraph ('Hence we can use the results of Schemes, Section 01JA to get a first order thickening Z ⊂ Z' over X'); Schemes, Lemmas 01JB, 01JC and the mapping property of the glued scheme

proof.text: *$Z\subset Z'$ is a first order thickening over $X$, and the $W_i$ are universal.* (a) $\iota^{-1}(W_j)=Z_j$: if $z\in Z_k$ and $\psi_k(\iota_k(z))\in W_j$, then $\iota_k(z)\in\psi_k^{-1}(W_k\cap W_j)=Z'_{kj}$, so $z\in Z_{kj}\subseteq Z_j$; the converse is clear. Under the isomorphism $\psi_j:Z'_j\to W_j$ the restriction $\iota|_{Z_j}:Z_j\to W_j$ is $\iota_j$, a closed immersion whose ideal sheaf has square zero. (b) Cover $Z'$ by affine opens $V$ each contained in some $W_j$; by part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] applied to $\iota_j$, each $\iota^{-1}(V)$ is affine and $\mathcal O_{Z'}(V)\to\mathcal O_Z(\iota^{-1}V)$ is surjective, so by part (2) $\iota$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. (c) Its ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_{Z'}\to\iota_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] restricts on $W_j$ to the ideal sheaf of $\iota|_{Z_j}$ (kernels of sheaf maps are computed open by open), whose square is $0$; a sheaf of ideals whose restriction to every member of an open covering is $0$ is $0$, so $\mathcal I^2=0$. With step 5 ($h'\circ\iota=h$), $Z\subset Z'$ with $h'$ is a first order thickening over $X$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. (d) By (a), $W_j$ is the open of $Z'$ with $\iota^{-1}(W_j)=Z_j$, and $(W_j,\iota|_{Z_j},h'|_{W_j})\cong(Z'_j,\iota_j,h'_j)$ via $\psi_j$, so $Z_j\subset W_j$ is a universal first order thickening of $Z_j$ over $X$ (step 2); similarly $W_j\cap W_k=\psi_j(Z'_{jk})$ is the open with $\iota^{-1}(W_j\cap W_k)=Z_{jk}$, and $Z_{jk}\subset W_j\cap W_k$ is a universal first order thickening of $Z_{jk}$ over $X$ (step 3).

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F3, end of the fourth paragraph ('a first order thickening Z ⊂ Z' over X which the property that the open subscheme Z'_i ⊂ Z' with Z_i = Z'_i ∩ Z is a universal first order thickening of Z_i over X'); closed immersions are checked on an affine covering, Morphisms, Lemma 01QO

proof.text: *The universal property of $Z'$.* Let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening over $X$ with closed immersion $i_T$ and $b:T'\to X$, and $a:T\to Z$ with $h\circ a=b\circ i_T$. Put $T_j=a^{-1}(Z_j)$, an open covering of $T$, and let $T'_j\subseteq T'$ be the open with $i_T^{-1}(T'_j)=T_j$; the $T'_j$ cover $T'$ since $i_T$ is a homeomorphism, and $T'_j\cap T'_k$ is the open over $T_j\cap T_k=a^{-1}(Z_{jk})$. By part (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-universal-thickening-open-pieces], $T_j\subset T'_j$ and $T_j\cap T_k\subset T'_j\cap T'_k$ are first order thickenings over $X$. *Existence:* by the universal property of $Z_j\subset W_j$ over $X$ (step 6 (d)) there is a unique $a'_j:T'_j\to W_j$ with $h'\circ a'_j=b|_{T'_j}$ and $a'_j\circ i_T|_{T_j}=\iota\circ a|_{T_j}$. On underlying sets $a'_j(i_T(t))=\iota(a(t))$, so $a'_j$ and $a'_k$ map $T'_j\cap T'_k$ into $W_j\cap W_k$ and factor through it [def-weil-open-immersion]; both are morphisms over $X$ restricting to $\iota\circ a$ on $T_j\cap T_k$, so by the uniqueness in the universal property of $Z_{jk}\subset W_j\cap W_k$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening] they agree on $T'_j\cap T'_k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] they glue to $a':T'\to Z'$, and $h'\circ a'=b$, $a'\circ i_T=\iota\circ a$ hold because they hold on every $T'_j$, resp. $T_j$ (uniqueness in the gluing lemma). *Uniqueness:* if $a'':T'\to Z'$ also satisfies $h'\circ a''=b$ and $a''\circ i_T=\iota\circ a$, then $a''(T'_j)=a''(i_T(T_j))=\iota(a(T_j))\subseteq W_j$, so $a''|_{T'_j}$ factors through $W_j$ and equals $a'_j$ by the uniqueness for $Z_j\subset W_j$; hence $a''=a'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. So $Z\subset Z'$ is a universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening].

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F3, last paragraph ('It turns out that this implies formally that Z' is a universal first order thickening of Z over X ... This finishes the proof')
